html:
In October 2010, nine months after the earthquake, cholera broke out in Haiti for the first time in at least a century. It killed about ten thousand people and sickened hundreds of thousands.

Scientists traced it to a base of United Nations peacekeepers from Nepal, where sewage leaked into a tributary of the Artibonite River, the country's main river. Few Haitians had clean water or toilets, so it spread fast.

The UN denied blame for years. In 2016 its Secretary-General apologised for the UN's part, but promised compensation was barely paid. The epidemic deepened distrust of foreign aid in Haiti. Cases ended by 2019, but cholera returned in 2022 amid the violence that followed the killing of President Moise.
sum: In October 2010, nine months after the earthquake, cholera broke out in Haiti for the first time in at least a century. It killed about ten thousand people and sickened hundreds of thousands.
